sections.sectionText: The Land Use Planning Workshop provides students with an immersive studio experience that applies advanced land use and urban design principles and skills to specific challenges in local jurisdictions. Building on the mapping and analysis skills learned in the Junior Planning Workshop, students will prepare professional quality plans for Park Ridge, Illinois. Students will explore and incorporate elements of legible city form, walkability, incrementalism, new (and old) urbanism, placemaking, activity generation, and missing middle housing into small area plans for various business districts and neighborhood centers within the community. Students will utilize ArcGIS, the Adobe Creative Suite, and SketchUp to prepare professional-quality plans and visualizations for future development. Special emphasis will be placed on learning and utilizing 3D visualization techniques throughout student work.

sections.sectionText: Subject: Using the Urbana campus as a living lab, students will learn about the Illinois Climate Action Plan and engage with campus stakeholders to recommend strategies to advance climate action on our campus. Students will work in groups to collect and analyze relevant data, conduct stakeholder interviews and focus groups, and write reports summarizing key challenges and opportunities to improve sustainability performance. (Juniors restricted from registering unless approval given by BAUSP Director.)

sections.sectionText: This seminar will explore theory, policy and practice of community engagement through cases studies, and observing actual planning and decision-making process at different scales and contexts. Students will learn about different tools and strategies that bring people together, particularly in low-income neighborhoods and culturally diverse cities. Collectively we will design a participatory process for a local organization. Throughout the semester we will grapple with the myriad of challenges and dilemmas faced by nonprofit advocates, community activists and equity-oriented public planners. Graduate students only.

sections.sectionText: Introduces the concepts, data, and methods used to assess environmental risk, vulnerability, and resilience in cities and regions. Examines how exposure, sensitivity, and adaptive capacity frame the real-world consequences of environmental hazards, and how these concepts are operationalized as indicators, composite indices, and maps. Students gain hands-on experience applying vulnerability indicators to a place of their choice using geospatial and statistical analysis tools, and learn how to communicate risks, vulnerabilities, and potential consequences to expert and non-technical audiences. 3 undergraduate hours. 3 graduate hours.

sections.sectionText: Title: Retrofitting Suburbia Using Small Area Plans The 54 acre Eastland Mall is a strategically important site east of downtown Bloomington, Illinois, that presents an interesting opportunity to apply planning ideas like “retrofitting suburbia” in the creation of a small area plan that describes how this site can evolve into a more sustainable, just, healthy, and community-serving place. Outputs from this workshop will include a polished professional small area type plan that synthesizes stakeholder input and background information and includes a development concept, site plan and implementation strategies. Students will also be expected to present this information to decision makers at the City of Bloomington.
